label: <DEL> step of long sequences that begin with d/w/0/f/z/c
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step: 96% of activation mass, and 12% of <DEL> steps are active. It never fires in the original phase, and only weakly at the first copy step or two. Activation rises with sequence length (L=9 > L=8 >> L<=7) and with whether the first original tokens, i.e. the token about to be output, are in {d, w, 0, f, z, c} (lift 4-7x for out_tok and first_tok). u and q are weaker members. The top examples all start with d, w or 0. The early tokens matter most: matching on token 0 or 1 does better than counting the set anywhere in the prefix. This looks like a graded sum of length and early-token identity, so a boolean predicate tops out around F1 0.6. Misses are shorter sequences (L=4-7) that start with set tokens, at low activation. False positives are long sequences whose leading tokens are set members but where the unit stays below threshold.
